unusual_experiment.name: INITIAL_GRANT_STATE_SYMLINK_ATTACK
unusual_experiment.baseline: Valid isolated one-time grant persists and second no-display launch reuses it without prompting.
unusual_experiment.intervention: Pre-create initial-grant-v1.json as a symlink to /dev/null inside an isolated EntityOS state root, then attempt deterministic test acceptance.
unusual_experiment.predicted_if_fail_closed: Exit 73, reject unsafe state, do not replace the symlink target.
unusual_experiment.rollback: Experiment used only an isolated temporary state tree; no user state or repository runtime state was modified.

grf_collapse.observed: The exact current one-file EntityOS artifact is independently reproducible on two existing Linux/X64 lanes and passes its canonical self-test plus an additional local exact-byte recheck.
grf_collapse.retained_hypothesis: The current one-file packaging and first-start grant boundary are strong enough to continue as the release carrier while deeper Clay Machine capability semantics are expanded.
grf_collapse.counter_reality: A one-file shell can still be functionally narrow or host-dependent even when packaging, local self-test and grant security pass.
grf_collapse.decision: RETAIN current EntityOS carrier; do not promote whole-machine acceptance.

release_blocker.exact_blocking_invariant: Whole-machine acceptance remains false because canonical Clay Bytes/Buffer ownership+lifetime and String/argv/effect-signature semantics plus broader network/media/runtime capability paths are not yet admitted through ClayCode -> TypedIR -> single ClayVM -> ClayOS.
release_blocker.next_executable_step: Implement and gate the smallest canonical String/Bytes/argv value and effect-signature slice that drives one real process request through the existing TypedIR/ClayVM/ClayOS path without prewired request-id semantics, then rebuild and re-test the exact one-file EntityOS.
